look: Chalk geometry: a dark maths-explainer look (3Blue1Brown-style): clean vector dots, arrows and grids drawn in glowing strokes on a dark ground, shapes morphing smoothly, short serif captions. Same look as the Poisson, Metrics, IER and MeshAnything films of this series.

scenes.name: Point2Mesh
scenes.desc: Title over our real Point2Mesh result turning slowly.

scenes.name: Shrink-wrap
scenes.desc: A loose wrap around dots is pulled tight until it hugs them.

scenes.name: The starting skin
scenes.desc: Our dots and the real convex hull of 2,000 triangles around them.

scenes.name: Pushing the corners
scenes.desc: Corners pushed freely chase every noisy dot and the skin turns jagged.

scenes.name: Let a network push
scenes.desc: A mesh network with one shared filter outputs every push; only its weights learn.

scenes.name: The self-prior
scenes.desc: The shared filter fits the overall shape before the noise.

scenes.name: What it minimises
scenes.desc: Gap to the dots, arrows that agree, and even triangles.

scenes.name: Coarse to fine
scenes.desc: Our real run: the hull shrinks onto the body, then gains triangles every 1,000 steps.

scenes.name: Part 1 in one line
scenes.desc: The method in five boxes, and what Part 2 covers.
